title: Squaring in your head
objectives: Square a two-digit number with $(a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2$
Recall the squares from 11 to 20, and rebuild one by stepping from a neighbour
Multiply two numbers the same distance either side of a round number with $(a - b)(a + b) = a^2 - b^2$

screens.prose: A square has side 13. Cut each side into 10 and 3, and it falls into four pieces.
screens.question: What is 13 × 13?

hints.text: Find the area of each of the four pieces.
There are two strips, each 10 by 3.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out all four pieces, then add them.

byKey.each-part: You squared 10 and 3 and added: 100 + 9. The two 10 by 3 strips add 60 more.
byKey.one-strip: You counted one strip. There are two, one along the top and one down the side.
byKey.doubled: You doubled 13. Squaring means 13 lots of 13.

explain.text: The pieces are $10^2 = 100$, two strips of $10 \times 3 = 30$, and a corner of $3^2 = 9$. Together, $13^2 = 169$. The two equal strips are what makes squaring quick.

screens.prose: Now let the units digit be any $b$ from 1 to 9. Slide it and watch the four pieces change.
screens.question: Whatever $b$ is, what do the two shaded strips add up to?

options.why: That is one strip. There are two of them, one along the top and one down the side.
That is the corner piece, $b$ by $b$. The strips are 10 by $b$.
That is the length of a side, not an area.

hints.text: Set $b$ to 4. What are the two strips then?
Each strip is 10 by $b$. There are two.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Each strip is 10 by $b$. Count how many there are.

explain.text: Each strip is $10 \times b$, and there are two, so they add to $20b$. Set $b = 4$: $(10 + 4)^2 = 100 + 80 + 16 = 196$. Double the units digit, put a zero on, and that is the middle piece.

screens.prose: You split the side, then added a square, two strips and a corner. In symbols that is $(a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2$, the **square of a sum**. Use it on 17.
screens.question: What is 17²?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add the square, both strips and the corner.

byKey.each-part: You squared 10 and 7 and added. The two strips, 70 each, are missing.
byKey.one-strip: You counted one strip of 70. There are two: $2 \times 70 = 140$.
byKey.corner-doubled: You doubled 7 for the corner. It is 7 by 7, so 49.

explain.text: The middle piece is $2 \times 10 \times 7 = 140$. So $17^2 = 100 + 140 + 49 = 289$. Say it in order: a hundred, plus a hundred and forty, plus forty-nine.

screens.prose: To step up from $n^2$, add a strip of $n$ on two sides and a corner of 1. So $(n + 1)^2 = n^2 + 2n + 1$.
screens.question: Step up from $15^2 = 225$ to fill in the squares to 20.

hints.text: Each step adds two strips of $n$ and a corner of 1.
Add 31, 33, 35, then 37: 256, 289, 324, 361. One more step, adding 39, lands on 400.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add $2n + 1$ to each square to get the next one.

explain.text: Each step adds the next odd number: 31, 33, 35, 37, then 39. Landing exactly on $20^2 = 400$ checks the whole column. Learn these squares by heart, and you can always rebuild one.

screens.prose: $19 \times 21$ is not a square. But 19 and 21 sit 1 either side of 20, so write it as $(20 - 1)(20 + 1)$. Hatched pieces are taken away.
screens.question: What is 19 × 21?

hints.text: Find the four pieces: two solid, two hatched.
The solid strip is $+20$ and the hatched strip is $-20$. They cancel.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add the solid pieces and take away the hatched ones.

byKey.no-corner: You let the strips cancel, which is right, but kept the corner. The corner is $-1 \times 1$, so take 1 off.
byKey.plus-corner: You added the corner. It is $-1 \times 1 = -1$, so it comes off.
byKey.low-square: That is $19^2$. Here one side is 21, which adds two more 19s: 38.
byKey.high-square: That is $21^2$. Here one side is 19, which takes off two 21s: 42.

explain.text: The strips $+20$ and $-20$ cancel, leaving $400 - 1 = 399$. Two numbers the same distance either side of a round number multiply to its square, less the gap squared. Here the gap is 1, so $1^2 = 1$ comes off.

screens.prose: Ravi squares 14 by squaring each part: $10^2 + 4^2 = 116$. Here is the square with side 14.
screens.question: Is Ravi right?

options.text: No. Two strips of 40 are missing, so it is 196
Yes. Square each part and add
options.why: You agreed with Ravi, who squared 10 and 4 and added. That keeps the square and the corner but drops the two 10 by 4 strips.

options.text: No. One strip of 40 is missing, so it is 156
options.why: You added one strip. There are two: one along the top and one down the side.
You doubled 4 for the corner. The corner is 4 by 4, so 16.

hints.text: $14^2$ is more than $12^2 = 144$. Can it be 116?
Look at the two pieces along the edges.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count all four pieces of the square.

byKey.ravi: You agreed with Ravi, who squared each part. That loses the two 10 by 4 strips, 80 in all.
byKey.one-strip: You added one strip of 40. There are two.
byKey.corner-doubled: You doubled 4 for the corner. It is 4 by 4, so 16.

explain.text: Ravi kept the square and the corner but lost both strips. $14^2 = 100 + 40 + 40 + 16 = 196$. Squaring a sum always has a middle piece: twice the product of the parts.

screens.prose: For two numbers the same distance either side of a round number, the strips always cancel. For any $a$ and $b$, $$(a - b)(a + b) = a^2 - b^2$$ Now give a reason for each line of $19 \times 21$.
screens.question: Put the lines in order.

lines.text: $19 \times 21 = (20 - 1)(20 + 1)$, write each as 20 and a step

hints.text: Which line still has 19 and 21 in it?
The four pieces come before any of them cancel.
Rewrite, multiply out, cancel the strips, then work out $400 - 1$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Start from the line that rewrites 19 and 21.

byKey.expand: That line multiplies out the brackets. Write the brackets first.
byKey.cancel: The strips can only cancel once all four pieces are written out.
byKey.finish: That is the answer, so it comes last.

explain.text: The strips are $+20$ and $-20$, so they cancel. What is left is $20^2 - 1^2$. For $18 \times 22$ the gap is 2, so $400 - 4 = 396$.

screens.prose: A stock's annual volatility is 18%, or 0.18. Its variance is the volatility squared. Square 18 first, then place the point.
screens.question: What is the variance, as a decimal?

hints.text: Square 18 first, then count decimal places.
$18^2 = 100 + 160 + 64 = 324$. Two places times two places gives four: 0.0324.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Square 18, then give the answer four decimal places.

byKey.point: You have the digits 324, but 0.18 has two decimal places. Its square has four: 0.0324.
byKey.each-part: You squared 0.1 and 0.08 and added. The two strips, 0.008 each, are missing.
byKey.whole: That is $18^2$. The volatility is 0.18, so place the decimal point.

explain.text: $18^2 = 100 + 160 + 64 = 324$. Since 0.18 has two decimal places, its square has four: $0.0324$. Variances of independent risks add and volatilities do not, so this square comes up all the time.

ideas: Split the side at a ten: $(10 + b)^2$ is 100, two strips of $10b$, and a corner of $b^2$.
Step to the next square by adding $2n + 1$: from $15^2 = 225$ to $16^2 = 256$.
For two numbers the same distance either side of a round number, the strips cancel: $19 \times 21 = 20^2 - 1^2 = 399$.

formula.name: The square of a sum
formula.note: And its partner: $(a - b)(a + b) = a^2 - b^2$.

summary.trap: Squaring each part drops the two strips: $14^2$ is 196, not $100 + 16 = 116$.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add 100, two strips of 60, and 36.

byKey.each-part: You squared 10 and 6 and added. The two strips, 60 each, are missing.
byKey.one-strip: You counted one strip of 60. There are two.
byKey.doubled: You doubled 16. Squaring means 16 lots of 16.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The gap from 20 is 2, so take off $2^2$.

byKey.gap-not-squared: You took off the gap, 2. The corner is 2 by 2, so take off 4.
byKey.no-corner: That is $20^2$. The corner $2^2 = 4$ still comes off.
byKey.one: You took off 1, as for $19 \times 21$. Here the gap is 2, so take off $2^2 = 4$.

explain.text: $18 \times 22 = (20 - 2)(20 + 2) = 20^2 - 2^2$. That is $400 - 4 = 396$. The gap is squared, so a gap of 2 costs 4.

quiz.prose: Traders turn daily volatility into annual volatility by multiplying by $\sqrt{252}$, for 252 trading days.
quiz.question: Which whole number is closest to $\sqrt{252}$?

options.why: You halved 252. A square root is the number that times itself gives 252.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Which of the squares up to $20^2$ is nearest 252?

explain.text: $16^2 = 256$ is only 4 above 252, while $15^2 = 225$ is 27 below. So $\sqrt{252} \approx 16$. A daily volatility of 1% is about 16% a year.
